newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL shares end mixed, secondaries lead rebound.
newsitem.headline: KL shares end mixed, secondaries lead rebound.

text.p: Shares closed mixed on Monday with the blue chip index finishing flat and small-capitalised stocks rebounding strongly, dealers said.
They said institutional investors remained wary at chasing up prices although shares have fallen to attractive prices after last week's market rout.
"I think Kuala Lumpur needs more time to consolidate. The volatile sessions will continue," said an institutional equity salesman at Jardine Fleming.
The key Composite Index closed down 0.52 of a point to 1,041.39.
The Second Board index jumped 19.81 or 3.84 percent to 535.88. "Sentiment is building up, but I'm afraid it may not be sustainble," said a retail dealer at Mayban Securities.
MBf Capital and Suria Capital were actively traded on renewed speculation of a merger between the two financial firms.
Most heavily traded MBf Capital jumped 32 cents to 4.58 on volume of 34.8 million shares. Dealers and analysts said they heard of share placements by the company at various prices.
Suria gained one cent to 2.59 on the fourth most-active volume of 6.7 million.
